findings.evidence: `NextResponse.redirect(new URL(url, req.nextUrl.origin), 302)`, where url is the relative '/api/media?...' path from LocalDriver.signedUrl. The age-verification return route uses env().APP_URL correctly.
findings.suggestedFix: Build the redirect with new URL(url, env().APP_URL), or return a relative Location.

findings.title: Age-verification return route turns provider fetch failures into a raw JSON 500/422 instead of redirecting to Settings
findings.scenario: A user finishes a Yoti check and is sent to /api/age-verification/return?sessionId=... If Yoti's result API returns non-2xx, takes longer than the 15 s timeout, or returns a shape that sessionResult.parse rejects (the adapter is unverified against the real service), fetchResult throws a plain Error or ZodError. The route rethrows anything that is not HttpError. route() then returns a 500 'internal' JSON body, or a 422 'Some fields need attention' with Yoti response field details. The user is left on a JSON page rather than being redirected to /settings#age-verification.
findings.evidence: route.ts:22 `if (!(err instanceof HttpError)) throw err;`. yotiRequest throws `new Error(...)` on !res.ok and AbortSignal timeouts propagate. route() maps ZodError to 422 with err.flatten().
findings.suggestedFix: Catch all errors in the return route, log the code only, and always redirect to VERIFY_PATH. The status stays pending and the webhook or next visit will settle it.

checkedAndFine: parseJson maps unparseable JSON to 400 invalid_json. Every JSON-body route parses with a zod schema that has string length caps, enums and array max sizes (draftSchema, paramsSchema .strict(), presetSchema, projectSchema/sceneSchema, takedownSchema, subscriptionSchema, publish/updateTemplateSchema, admin schemas).
route() returns ZodError as 422 with flatten() (field messages, no stack) and unknown errors as a generic 500 message. No stack trace or SQL appears in any response body.

Invalid UUID path params (projects, scenes, folders, presets, characters, consents, generations, admin ids) reach Postgres as 22P02, which isBadIdentifier walks through DrizzleQueryError.cause and maps to 404. GET /api/generations/[id] regex-checks the id first.

Pagination: /api/templates caps offset at 10000 and limit at 60. listCreations caps limit at 200. Presets are capped at 100, characters at 20, scenes per project at 50, folder add at 100 ids per call.
Numeric ranges: seed 0..2^31-1, durationS 1..60, motionIntensity 1..10, rating 1..5, admin credit adjust +/-100000 non-zero, priceMultiplierPct 10..1000, confirm expectedCost int>=0 (compared only).

Storage keys: LocalDriver.safeLocalPath enforces a strict regex and a root-prefix check. /api/media requires an HMAC over key+exp+download with timingSafeEqual, refuses non-clean or deleted assets, and strips the download filename to [\w.-] for Content-Disposition (no header injection).
Range parsing in /api/media handles suffix, open-ended, out-of-range and empty-file cases with 416.

Webhooks: payments, age-verification and Replicate read the raw body and verify signatures before use. webhookParams JSON parse errors are mapped to 400 malformed. __proto__ keys in webhook bodies cannot pollute (string assignment to __proto__ is ignored).
Push subscription endpoints are restricted to known push-service hosts over https with no port or userinfo (no SSRF). p256dh and auth lengths are validated.
Search q escapes % and _ for ILIKE, and the pattern always ends in '%', so there is no 'pattern ends with escape' error.

Logger calls outside route(): payment, age, scan, push and generation logs carry ids, codes and statuses only (no prompts, emails, tokens or media bytes). The takedown audit row stores only the category and target type.

ApiError.verifyPath on the client comes only from the server's VERIFY_PATH constant. The age-verification return route builds both redirects from env().APP_URL. The verify/sandbox and pricing/sandbox pages encode their auth next values and return 404/redirect when not in sandbox or on a live deployment.
Sandbox payment token: HMAC-checked, JSON and zod parsing in try/catch, user-bound. The pricing sandbox route checks refund and chargeback references against the user's own payment rows.
Middleware CSRF origin check covers mutating /api routes except webhooks. Cookies are httpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
JSON bodies are effectively capped at 10 MB by the middleware body clone. Truncated JSON yields 400, not 500.

findings.title: A refund or chargeback that arrives before its purchase is dropped for good, and the purchase still grants credits when it lands
findings.scenario: 1) A CCBill NewSaleSuccess for pack_large (1200 credits) gets a 5xx during a deploy or DB blip, so CCBill queues a retry. 2) The sale is voided or refunded the same day, or the buyer files a chargeback. That Refund/Void/Chargeback webhook arrives first. 3) clawback() finds no credited event, so it returns outcome 'ignored' with metadata reason 'original_not_found'. The payment_events row is committed and we answer 200. 4) The NewSaleSuccess retry arrives and grant() adds 1200 credits. 5) If the processor sends the refund again, the unique (provider, provider_event_id) row makes it 'duplicate'. Result: the buyer keeps credits for money they got back. For a chargeback, no 'chargeback' account flag is written either, so assertCanCheckout keeps checkout open. Nothing in src/ or scripts/ reprocesses 'original_not_found' rows (I grepped and found none). The same ordering hole applies to a subscription: a cancellation for a subscription not yet seen is 'ignored' (line 126), and the later subscription_started inserts it as active.
findings.evidence: processPaymentEvent inserts the event row with onConflictDoNothing and commits whatever apply() returns. clawback() returns a normal 'ignored' result, not an error, when findCreditedEvent() returns null. In contrast, subscription_renewed deliberately throws when its parent is missing (lines 98-100), so the transaction rolls back and the processor retries. Reversals get no such treatment. grant() never looks for earlier reversals of the same transactionRef.
findings.suggestedFix: When the original is not found, throw, as the renewal path does. The insert of the event row then rolls back and the processor redelivers until the purchase exists. Or store the reversal as pending and have the purchase/subscription_started path apply any pending reversals with a matching transactionRef/subscriptionRef in the same transaction. Do the same for subscription_cancelled/updated on an unknown subscription.

findings.title: updateTemplate writes back a status read before its transaction, so a concurrent edit undoes a moderation removal or suspension
findings.scenario: 1) A creator whose template has been reported runs a loop that sends parallel no-op PATCH /api/templates/:id {"title":"x"}. 2) Request R1 reads t.status='published' at line 153, outside any transaction. 3) The admin resolves the report with 'remove' (admin.ts:119 sets status='removed') and it commits. 4) R1's transaction runs UPDATE templates SET status = input.status ?? t.status ('published'), with no status condition in the WHERE, and the template is public again. Discovery's 'published' filter checks only status and deletedAt, not the creator's account status. The same interleaving undoes suspendUser's unpublish (admin.ts:215-219): requests already past requireUser complete after the sessions are destroyed. It also undoes the template takedown that recordVerdict does when a public asset matches the abuse scanner (scan/index.ts:167-172). With many requests in flight, nearly every removal lands inside some request's read-to-write window. The same stale read also loses updates: an edit that changes only the title writes back the old currentVersion after a concurrent prompt edit created version N+1, so the template silently reverts to the old prompt. Two concurrent prompt edits both insert version N+1 and hit template_versions_uq, which surfaces as a 500.
findings.evidence: The template is read with getDb() outside the transaction, and the 'removed' check happens on that stale row. The transaction writes every column from the stale row (status, currentVersion, title, tags, isVip...) with .where(eq(templates.id, t.id)) only. There is no FOR UPDATE and no optimistic version check.
findings.suggestedFix: Inside the transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE the template, re-check status <> 'removed' (and the creator's status) under the lock, compute the next version from the locked row, and write only the fields actually supplied. Add AND status <> 'removed' to the UPDATE as a backstop. Only an explicit input.status may change the status.

findings.title: If recording an abuse-scan match fails, the worker deletes the matched output's bytes immediately: no hold, no escalation, no suspension
findings.scenario: An output matches PhotoDNA. scanAsset → recordVerdict opens its match transaction: it locks the asset row FOR UPDATE, inserts the escalation, flag and audit rows, and for a CSAM match runs UPDATE users SET status='suspended'. Any exception in that transaction rolls it back, so legal_hold stays false. Causes include a DB connection reset or failover, a statement timeout, or a deadlock. One concrete deadlock: the owner's deleteAccount transaction has already updated (locked) the users row and is waiting on the same media_assets row in its UPDATE media_assets ... WHERE owner_id=... AND legal_hold=false, while the match transaction holds the asset and waits on the users row. The exception propagates out of storeAndSettle to processJob's catch, which calls discardAfterFault(track). The asset was added to track.assetIds by recorded() before the scan (line 281), so discardStored soft-deletes it (legal_hold=false matches) and purgeAssetsNow deletes the file at once. Then finishFailed refunds the job as 'internal'. Net effect: CSAM evidence destroyed, nothing in the review queue, account not suspended, user refunded.
findings.evidence: recorded(key, asset.id) runs before scanAsset. The catch at 219-227 discards everything in track without checking whether the asset's scan finished. discardStored and purgeAssetsNow only spare rows whose legal_hold is already true, and the match transaction that would have set it rolled back.
findings.suggestedFix: Never purge an asset whose scan did not complete. Remove the current asset from track before calling scanAsset and leave it as scan_status 'pending' (never served; scan-backfill rescans it), or wrap scanAsset so an exception is treated as 'unavailable' without deleting bytes, and alert. Also take the users row lock before the asset lock in recordVerdict (or lock in a consistent order) to remove the deadlock with deleteAccount.

findings.title: Two reversals of the same payment processed concurrently both claw back the full amount
findings.scenario: A user bought pack_medium (550 credits, $44.99) and holds 1000 credits. A full refund and a chargeback (or two reversal events with different ids) for that transaction are processed at the same time. T1 and T2 each sum earlier reversals (lines 171-174) before either has committed, so alreadyReversed=0 and owed=550 for both. They then serialize on the credit_accounts FOR UPDATE (line 184). T1 reverses 550, leaving 450. T2 gets the lock and, under READ COMMITTED, sees available=450, but still uses its stale owed=550, so it reverses 450 and writes a credit_debt flag for a 100-credit 'shortfall'. The user loses 1000 credits for one $44.99 reversal. Processed one after the other, T2 would have computed owed=0.
findings.evidence: The 'earlier' aggregate reads payment_events rows whose reversesEventId is only set in the final UPDATE of each transaction, and it runs before the only lock taken (the account row). Nothing locks the original purchase event.
findings.suggestedFix: Lock first, then read. SELECT the original payment_events row FOR UPDATE (or the credit account) before computing 'earlier', so the second reversal sees the first one's committed row.

findings.title: The active-jobs cap is checked before any lock, so parallel confirms exceed it (a paid perk)
findings.scenario: A free user (USER_MAX_ACTIVE_JOBS=3) with 2 active jobs creates 5 drafts and fires 5 POST /api/generations/:id/confirm requests in parallel. Each transaction locks only its own job row and runs count(*) of queued and processing jobs, sees 2, and passes. The first lock shared by all of them is the credit_accounts FOR UPDATE inside reserveForJob, which comes after the check. All 5 queue (7 active), as long as credits cover them. 'N generations at once' is sold as a pass perk (pricing.ts: 3 or 6), and one user can fill the shared worker queue ahead of everyone else.
findings.evidence: The count query runs before reserveForJob → lockAccount, so concurrent confirms for one user are not serialized at the point of the check.
findings.suggestedFix: Take the per-user lock before counting: call lockAccount (SELECT credit_accounts ... FOR UPDATE) or pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(user_id)) at the start of the confirm transaction, then count.

findings.title: A processor 'Cancellation' (stop rebilling) ends the paid pass immediately instead of at period end
findings.scenario: A user buys the Studio Pass on day 1 and on day 2 cancels the auto-renewal at CCBill or Segpay, which is common. CCBill sends Cancellation now and Expiration at the end of the period. Segpay sends Cancellation now and Disable at expiry. Both adapters map the cancellation itself to subscription_cancelled, and processPaymentEvent sets status='canceled'. activePlan() counts only active/trialing rows, so VIP templates and the 6-job concurrency stop on day 2, although the user paid through day 30.
findings.evidence: CCBill maps both 'Cancellation' and 'Expiration', and Segpay maps 'cancel'/'cancellation' alongside 'disable', to the same subscription_cancelled event. The handler sets status canceled no matter what current_period_end says, and activePlan filters on status before period end.
findings.suggestedFix: Map 'stop rebilling' events (CCBill Cancellation, Segpay Cancellation) to a status that stays entitled until current_period_end, for example status 'active' with a cancelAtPeriodEnd marker. Only Expiration/Disable should end access.

findings.title: Account deletion leaves the processor subscription billing, and renewals keep granting credits to the deleted account
findings.scenario: A Night Pass holder deletes their account in Settings. deleteAccount soft-deletes content and sessions but never touches the subscriptions row or calls the provider. The optional cancelSubscription is not called anywhere, and the deletion sheet says nothing about passes. Each month CCBill/Segpay rebills the card, and subscription_renewed grants 400 credits to an account nobody can sign in to.
findings.evidence: deleteAccount has no subscriptions update and no provider call. The renewal handler looks up the subscription by provider id and grants to sub.userId without checking users.status or deleted_at.
findings.suggestedFix: In deleteAccount, mark the user's subscriptions canceled and either call provider.cancelSubscription or block deletion until the pass is cancelled at the processor, with that explained in the deletion sheet. Ignore or refund renewals for deleted users.

findings.title: Favorite and rating counters drift under concurrency despite the 'can never drift' comment
findings.scenario: T1 and T2 favorite the same template at once. Each inserts its row, then runs UPDATE templates SET favorite_count = (SELECT count(*) ...). Under READ COMMITTED, T2's count subquery uses T2's statement snapshot, taken before T1 committed. T2 waits for T1's row lock and then writes count = n+1 although there are n+2 favorites. rateTemplate's rating_sum and rating_count drift the same way. The counts correct themselves on the next change but can stay wrong indefinitely for a template nobody touches again.
findings.evidence: There is no lock on the template before counting. The recount subquery is not re-run against the newer snapshot after the row-lock wait.
findings.suggestedFix: Lock the template row first (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) before the insert and recount, or use atomic +1/-1 based on whether the insert or delete affected a row.

findings.title: The worker ignores deleted_at, so a job soft-deleted while queued runs and charges
findings.scenario: deleteJob reads the job outside a transaction (status awaiting_confirmation), and the same user's confirm in another tab commits 'queued' in between. deleteJob's transaction then sets deleted_at without re-checking status. processJob claims only on status='queued' and never looks at deleted_at, so the job runs and settleJob charges it. The Library hides it, and cancelJob filters deleted_at and returns 404, so the user cannot stop it. resolveTakedown on a job id that is still queued or processing has the same effect: it sets deleted_at without cancelRequested, so the output is created afterwards, unhidden and unheld, and the CSAM branch had no assets to hold.
findings.evidence: deleteJob does check-then-act across two statements with no FOR UPDATE. The claim transaction in processJob tests only status and cancelRequested.
findings.suggestedFix: In deleteJob, lock the row and re-check status inside the transaction. Have every soft-delete of a job also set cancel_requested=true, and have processJob treat deleted_at IS NOT NULL like cancelRequested (release and cancel).

findings.title: The purge job can delete bytes of an asset put on legal hold after its candidate SELECT
findings.scenario: The hourly purgeDeletedMedia selects up to 500 soft-deleted rows with legal_hold=false, then deletes them one at a time. While it iterates, an admin actions a CSAM takedown on one of those assets: legal_hold=true is set and an escalation opened. purgeRows still calls storage().delete(key) and overwrites storage_key with 'purged/<id>', so the escalation points at evidence that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: purgeRows neither re-checks legal_hold nor locks the row. Its final UPDATE has no legal_hold condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Per row, first run UPDATE media_assets SET storage_key='purged/'||id WHERE id=$1 AND legal_hold=false AND storage_key=$key RETURNING, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and delete the bytes only if that claimed the row.

findings.title: startVerification can overwrite a just-verified status with 'pending'
findings.scenario: A user completes check A at the provider, then clicks Verify again before A's callback arrives. startVerification B reads status 'pending' and awaits provider.start. A's callback commits status 'verified'. B's transaction then runs an unconditional UPDATE users SET age_verification_status='pending'. The user is blocked from explicit content again until B completes, and if B is abandoned and later fails, the status becomes 'failed'. This only harms the user themselves; it is not a bypass.
findings.evidence: The status check happens before the provider call. The users update at line 119 has no status condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Add WHERE age_verification_status <> 'verified' to the users update at line 119 (as the failure path already does), or skip it if the row is verified.

checkedAndFine: Credit ledger: applyMovement locks credit_accounts FOR UPDATE before its idempotency lookup. Two concurrent confirms of drafts the balance cannot both cover serialize there; the second throws InsufficientCreditsError and its whole confirm transaction (status change included) rolls back. CHECK constraints also forbid negative balances.
Settle and release share the key job:<id>:close, so a job is closed exactly once, never both charged and refunded.

Duplicate concurrent payment webhooks: payment_events is unique on (provider, provider_event_id) and the insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inside the transaction. The second delivery waits for the first to commit and returns 'duplicate'. If the first rolls back (renewal before start), the second processes normally.
createDraft idempotency: unique (user_id, idempotency_key), insert ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then re-read the winner.

confirmJob, cancelJob, the processJob claim, finishFailed and the worker's final commit all lock the job row FOR UPDATE and re-check status, so confirm vs cancel vs claim vs completion interleavings resolve correctly.
The reconcile draft sweep is an UPDATE ... WHERE status='awaiting_confirmation'. Postgres re-checks the condition after the row-lock wait, so a draft confirmed concurrently is not expired.

retryOrFail only moves processing→queued (WHERE status='processing'), so a job already closed by the reconciler or a cancel is not revived. Extra queue entries are harmless because processJob claims only 'queued', and queue ids include the attempt number.

Scanner outage with fail-closed: unscanned bytes are deleted, the job is requeued with its reservation held, and finishFailed refunds once attempts run out. A reconciler timeout during a long scan refunds and discards the late outputs under the job lock.

Matched output on the normal path: legal_hold is set in the same transaction as scan_status='matched'. discardStored and purgeAssetsNow both filter legal_hold=false, and deleteAccount, withdrawConsent and non-CSAM takedowns skip held assets.

Account deletion while jobs run: every job gets cancel_requested. Queued jobs release at claim; processing jobs release through the cancel watch or at the final commit. The final commit soft-deletes outputs stored after the deletion.

withdrawConsent concurrent with confirm: the job UPDATE waits for confirm's row lock and then sets cancel_requested, so the worker releases. The worker re-validates inputs (deleted_at, scan_status clean, consent) at execution, so a withdrawn upload or reference never reaches the provider.

Push subscriptions: the endpoint is unique and the upsert hands an endpoint to the latest signed-in user and session. deliverableSubscriptions requires a live session of that same user, and logout removes rows (and the FK cascades).
resolveEscalation, resolveTakedown and resolveReport lock their row FOR UPDATE and reject an item that is already resolved, so two admins cannot double-apply.
Age applyResult locks the verification row, treats anything not pending as a replay, and a failure never downgrades a verified account.

Migration 0003 (SET NULL FKs): users, jobs, templates, payment events and media assets are only soft-deleted, so those SET NULL actions never fire in normal flows. Scene hard-deletes null generation_jobs.scene_id, and confirmJob handles a null sceneId or parentJobId.
Clawback never drives available negative: the reversed amount is capped by available, and the shortfall becomes a credit_debt flag.
reorderScenes locks the scene rows. selectVersion runs in a transaction and requires the version's job to be completed and not deleted.

I did not run any of these interleavings. A scratch Postgres for demonstrating them could not be started because of scratchpad directory permissions, so every finding comes from reading the code at f8d5ef3.

findings.title: With STORAGE_DRIVER=s3, signed media links skip every serve-time check, so taken-down or deleted media stays downloadable after removal (up to 1 hour for public media, 5 minutes for private)
findings.scenario: Setup: production runs with STORAGE_DRIVER=s3, the S3/MinIO option the infra compose profile supports. (1) A creator publishes template T. Every explore, home, template and creator page render calls assetUrl(), which returns a presigned S3 GET URL valid for 3600 s. Each adult viewer receives one in the HTML or RSC payload. (2) Someone files a takedown on T with category csam, and an admin takes it down. resolveTakedown sets deletedAt and legalHold on T's poster and preview. Because the assets are held, purgeAssetsNow and purgeDeletedMedia never delete the S3 object. (3) Every presigned URL issued in the previous hour still returns the bytes directly from the bucket until it expires. Anyone holding one (any viewer, a scraper, or someone they forwarded it to) can download and re-share the reported content for up to 60 minutes after the takedown. The same gap applies when a moderator removes a template from the Reports panel (assets are never even marked), and to account or creation deletion ('hides it at once' per the Policies page) for the length of the retention window. The deletedAt/scanStatus checks in /api/media, which docs/abuse-response.md:39 names as the control ('404 ... even with a validly signed link issued earlier'), run only for the local driver.
findings.evidence: S3Driver.signedUrl calls getSignedUrl(GetObjectCommand) with expiresIn: ttl, so the browser goes straight to the bucket and app code never runs again. assetUrl uses ttl = 3600 for public assets (media.ts:29). The only per-request check (deletedAt, scanStatus === 'clean') is in src/app/api/media/route.ts:23, which only LocalDriver URLs reach. The CSAM takedown branch (takedowns.ts:193) sets deletedAt plus legalHold and adds the assets to no purge list. purgeAssetsNow and purgeDeletedMedia both filter legal_hold = false, so the object, and every URL that points at it, stays alive. S3 objects are also put without CacheControl, and presigned URLs set no ResponseCacheControl. The local route sends 'private'; S3 sends nothing.
findings.suggestedFix: Make removal revoke links on S3. When an asset is held, taken down, removed or deleted, move the object to a new key (for example CopyObject to evidence/<assetId>, DeleteObject on the old key, then update storageKey). Old presigned URLs then 404 while the evidence survives. Alternatively, serve S3 media through /api/media, or a CDN with signed cookies that checks the DB, instead of handing out bucket URLs. Shorten the public TTL. Pass ResponseCacheControl: 'private, no-store' when presigning. Correct docs/abuse-response.md:39 to match.

findings.title: Removing a template from the Reports panel, or suspending its creator, leaves its media servable through links already handed out (up to about 2 hours on the default local driver)
findings.scenario: A member reports a published template with reason 'minor' or 'non_consent'. An admin resolves the report with action 'remove'. resolveReport only sets templates.status = 'removed'. The template's public poster and preview media rows keep deletedAt = null and scanStatus = 'clean'. Each viewer who loaded explore, home, the template page or a creator page in the previous 1 to 2 hours holds a signed /api/media URL. The media route accepts any valid signature for a clean, non-deleted asset, so those URLs keep returning the image or video, with 'Cache-Control: private, max-age=<remaining>' so browsers keep it too. Public links are signed with exp = ceil((now+3600)/3600)*3600, so they last 3600 to 7199 s. suspendUser behaves the same way (it sets templates to 'unpublished' only). The takedown path does soft-delete the assets (takedowns.ts:206), so the two removal paths are inconsistent. The removed template's files are also never soft-deleted, so they are never purged.
findings.evidence: admin.ts:119 updates only templates. No mediaAssets update exists for subjectType 'template'; the 'output' branch at :121-122 does update media. The media route checks only `asset.deletedAt` and `asset.scanStatus !== 'clean'` (route.ts:23). It does not check visibility, template status or owner status. LocalDriver.signedUrl rounds expiry up to the next TTL boundary (storage/index.ts:60). I checked the arithmetic with node: lifetimes are 3600 to 7197 s for public links and 300 to 599 s for private ones.
findings.suggestedFix: In resolveReport's template 'remove' branch and in suspendUser, soft-delete the template's posterAssetId and previewAssetId. For SEVERE reasons such as 'minor', place them on legal hold and open an escalation, as resolveTakedown does. Optionally have /api/media refuse public assets whose template is no longer published.

findings.title: Signup confirms whether an email has an account, and the IP rate limit is keyed on a client-supplied header
findings.scenario: An attacker wants to know whether a specific person (partner, coworker) uses this adults-only site. They POST /api/auth/signup with that person's email, a random handle, an adult date of birth and both checkboxes. Response 409 {code:'email_taken', message:'That email already has an account.'} means the person is a member. Response 201 means they are not; the attacker then deletes the throwaway account with DELETE /api/me using the password they chose. Suspended accounts are revealed too, because only deleted accounts get their email rewritten. Ten probes an hour per IP is enough for targeted outing. The limit key is the first X-Forwarded-For value, which the client controls when no proxy overwrites it (no reverse proxy is bundled). Rotating that header therefore allows bulk enumeration. The login path takes care to avoid this leak (dummy-hash timing, one generic 401), so signup undoes it.
findings.evidence: registerUser catches the users_email_uq unique violation and throws HttpError(409, 'email_taken', ...) with a field error (account.ts:93). The signup route sets ip = x-forwarded-for.split(',')[0] and calls rateLimit(`signup:${ip}`, 10, 3600) (route.ts:9-10). No email verification step exists, so a probe against an unregistered email also creates an account under someone else's address.
findings.suggestedFix: Return the same response for new and existing emails, and send an email to the address instead: either a 'verify your account' link, or 'someone tried to sign up with your email'. Activate accounts only after email verification. Key the rate limit on the address the trusted edge reports (or the rightmost XFF hop added by your proxy), and add a per-email limit.

findings.title: A VIP template's full recipe (prompt, negative prompt, model, settings) is sent to and shown to viewers without a pass, and the same generation succeeds without the templateId
findings.scenario: A signed-in member without a pass opens /templates/<vip-slug>. The page computes locked = true and shows the 'A pass unlocks it' banner. It still passes prompt: data.version.prompt, negativePrompt, modelKey and defaults to CreatePanel, which preloads them into the visible, editable prompt textarea. The member copies them into /generate/image and submits with no templateId. createDraft checks VIP only inside `if (input.templateId)`, so the same recipe runs on the same model and the VIP gate is bypassed. If the recipe is meant to be the paid part of a VIP template, this delivers paid content without payment. If prompts are meant to be public teasers, the gate only blocks attribution. Product owner to decide; payments reviewers may already cover this.
findings.evidence: template page: `const locked = t.isVip && !ctx.vip && !data.own;` then `template={{ ..., prompt: data.version.prompt, negativePrompt: data.version.negativePrompt, modelKey: data.version.modelKey, defaults: ..., locked }}`. create-panel: `prompt: prefill?.prompt ?? template?.prompt ?? ""` → useState(original.prompt), rendered in the textarea whether or not the template is locked. service.ts:236 throws vip_required only when templateId is set.
findings.suggestedFix: When `locked`, leave prompt, negativePrompt and defaults out of the page and RSC payload (send the title and model only), and show the recipe after purchase. If the recipe is meant to be public, say so on the pricing page and rename the gate so it does not suggest the recipe is paid content.

findings.title: 'Remix of' line shows the title and slug of a source template that was later unpublished, removed by moderation or takedown, or deleted with its creator's account
findings.scenario: Creator X publishes template A titled with identifying text, for example a real person's name. Member Y makes something from A and publishes it as template B, so B.remixedFromId = A. Later A is taken down as NCII (status removed, deletedAt set), or X deletes their account, or X unpublishes A. Anyone viewing B, including signed-out and unverified viewers, still sees 'Remix of <A's title>' and a link containing A's slug. The text that the takedown, deletion or unpublish was meant to withdraw stays public on someone else's page.
findings.evidence: templateForViewer loads remixedFrom with `select({ slug, title }).from(templates).where(eq(templates.id, row.t.remixedFromId))`. It has no status = 'published' or deletedAt filter. The page renders data.remixedFrom.title and the slug link whenever the row exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `eq(templates.status, 'published'), isNull(templates.deletedAt)` to the remixedFrom lookup. Otherwise render a neutral 'Remix of a template that is no longer available'.

findings.title: Signed links last up to twice as long as the Policies page states, and stay in the browser cache for that time
findings.scenario: The Policies page tells users a private link 'lasts five minutes by default'. LocalDriver.signedUrl rounds expiry up to the next multiple of the TTL. A private link signed at 10:00:01 expires at 10:10:00 (599 s), and a public link signed at 10:00:01 expires at 12:00:00 (7199 s, not 1 hour). The media route then sends Cache-Control: private, max-age=<remaining>, so a shared browser keeps the bytes for that whole span. A user relying on the stated 5-minute window when sharing a link (which the page warns about) gets up to 10 minutes.
findings.evidence: `const exp = Math.ceil((now + ttlSeconds) / ttlSeconds) * ttlSeconds;` I checked the lifetimes with node: 300 to 599 s private, 3600 to 7197 s public. route.ts:29 sets max-age to exp minus now.
findings.suggestedFix: Round to a sub-window instead (for example ceil to 60 s) so a link lasts at most TTL + 60 s, or change the Policies text to say 'up to ten minutes'. Consider 'private, no-store' on private media rather than max-age.

checkedAndFine: buildPushPayload (src/server/push/payload.ts) builds the payload from the outcome and a UUID job id only, with fixed text such as 'Your creation is ready'. web-push encrypts with aes128gcm. notify.ts logs ids and counts, never endpoints. In sw.js, notificationFrom clamps title, body and tag, and accepts only same-origin relative URLs.

Push subscriptions are tied to the session (saveSubscription), removed on logout (logout route) and cascade-deleted with the session row. deliverableSubscriptions sends only to devices with an unexpired session of the same user. The endpoint host allowlist blocks using the push sender to reach arbitrary hosts (SSRF).

Service worker (public/sw.js): routeFor sends /api/* (including /api/media), Range requests, cross-origin and non-GET requests to the network without answering them. shouldCache stores only /_next/static, /icons and the shell URLs, never page HTML, and never a 200 marked private or no-store. The navigation fallback is only the /offline copy fetched with credentials: 'omit', which the root layout renders with no shell (layout.tsx:44-50). /generate, /creators and / are missing from PRIVATE_PREFIXES, but that is harmless because shouldCache never stores navigations.

Pages: Next sends 'private, no-cache, no-store' for dynamic pages, and the build's prerender-manifest (/home/claude/hushloom/.next) has no prerendered routes. API JSON responses set no Cache-Control but carry no ETag or Last-Modified, so browsers do not cache them heuristically. /api/media sets 'private'.

Local /api/media: an HMAC over key, expiry and download name, checked in constant time. It re-checks deletedAt and scanStatus on every request and sanitizes Content-Disposition. Production refuses to boot without MEDIA_SIGNING_SECRET (env.ts:116).
assetUrl signs only clean, non-deleted assets that are public or owned by the viewer. All call sites pass the real viewer id. creatorAnalytics signs as the creator but runs only when isOwner.

Upload metadata: images are decoded and re-encoded to WebP with sharp, which drops EXIF, GPS and XMP. Videos are rewritten with ffmpeg -map_metadata -1 -map_chapters -1 -c copy; default stream selection drops data tracks. Both happen before storage or scan.

Template publishing is an explicit act and the UI says the prompt becomes public. It refuses jobs with inputAssetIds (so continuations of own clips are refused too) or a character reference, and refuses outputs that are not clean or are held. It copies the output to a new public asset; the original stays private.

Remix and reuse prefill (generatePrefill), deriveDraft, lineage, getCreation, listCreations (including the folder and template-creator filters, which stay inside the user's own jobs), libraryFacets, projects and characters are all scoped to the user id.
Creator pages show only published templates and public collections. Owner analytics and current prompts render only for the owner.

Metadata: a template page's <title> uses templateForViewer(id, null), so only published titles appear. Collection, project, settings and admin pages use static titles. Layout metadata sets robots noindex, and next.config adds X-Robots-Tag.
Referrer-Policy is strict-origin-when-cross-origin, pages load no third-party subresources, and signed URLs never appear in page URLs, so signed links do not leak via Referer.
Admin abuse review never displays matched media. The owner email and requester email shown to admins are what reporting needs.
Takedown endpoint returns 201 whatever the target, and its audit row stores only ids and the category.

Logs at f8d5ef3: http.ts:69 serializes a DrizzleQueryError's message and stack, which contain the bound params (prompts, emails). HEAD 3412ad0 fixes this with redactQueryParams in src/server/log.ts (infra track). Next's own error printer is already a listed open issue, so this is not re-reported.
No src/instrumentation.ts or error webhook exists in the snapshot; both arrive with infra at HEAD and get their own pass.

No dangerouslySetInnerHTML and React escaping throughout. There is no page CSP, which is hygiene only since no injection sink was found. The configured providers (demo, flux-schnell) do not return SVG output.
Browser storage: only the per-tab push resync marker (sessionStorage). No prompts or drafts are written to localStorage.
